sections.title: Current conclusion
sections.markdown:
**HOLD —** the printed Edinburgh apprenticeship register names John Glasgow
under its explicit Glasgow heading on 12 January 1648. It identifies William
Blackwood, merchant, as his master and describes the apprentice as the son of
the late “Thomas G., maltman, burgess of Glasgow.” The father's surname is
abbreviated in the line. The entry proves an apprenticeship occurrence, not a
birth or death date, and does not identify a particular WikiTree profile.

Keep this as a separate, searchable record subject. Glasgow-1604, Glasgow-3145
and Glasgow-3610 remain chronologically possible John profiles. Creating another
WikiTree profile now risks duplication. Thomas Glasgow-1103 is only a possible
lead for the father; his occupation and relationship are unproved.

sections.title: Identity and relationship assessment
sections.markdown:
- **John Glasgow as a named apprentice:** documented by the printed heading and entry.
- **Father Thomas G.:** documented as deceased by the entry date and described as a maltman and burgess of Glasgow. The printed line abbreviates his surname; no living or historic Thomas profile has been connected to him.
- **Glasgow-1604:** possible by chronology, but no Thomas, occupation or apprenticeship link.
- **Glasgow-3145:** possible by chronology, but no distinguishing link; may duplicate Glasgow-1604.
- **Glasgow-3610:** possible by chronology, but its stated Kirknewton/East Calder context and attached father William do not match this record; those profile details are not fully sourced.
- **Thomas Glasgow-1103 as father:** possible age-wise, but occupation, burgess status and parent-child link are absent; his uncertain later death does not settle the question.
- Other reviewed Johns have a stated incompatible father/locality, are likely an infant, or are too young. No profile attachment or new WikiTree profile is recommended now.

sections.title: Recommended next records
sections.markdown:
- Search Glasgow burgess and maltmen records for Thomas G. and his household.
- Look for a surviving record of the original apprenticeship register or a related merchant record naming John with a residence, occupation, kin or associates.
- Compare any new identifier with the household evidence for Glasgow-1604, Glasgow-3145 and Glasgow-3610 before attaching or creating a WikiTree profile.

potential_parentage.method: Automated leads use birth surnames—not married surnames—as parental eligibility, role-specific biological age limits, bounded and approximate-date uncertainty, household chronology, specific time-aware localities, mapped distance, tenancy succession, migration destinations and sex-aware Scottish naming positions across generations. People already attached as the subject's parents stay in the identity summary and are excluded from this alternative-candidate list, regardless of relationship confidence. The main calibration uses clues available on disconnected profiles; existing parent and sibling links are retained as comparison context rather than treated as transferable evidence. Common ordered names and grandparent-to-child echoes receive a small non-zero weight, so a John or James match can support several independent criteria without producing a lead alone. Rare names, repeated bearers and bundles across otherwise distinct branches receive substantially more weight according to catalogue frequency. An exact migration place is weighted by its rarity and repetition across both branches; a shared destination country is worth only one point. Extra weight is added only when at least three independent clue types converge: naming, locality, specific migration, household chronology or collateral networks. Sparse profiles retain a clearly labelled chronology-only fallback instead of disappearing. Countries, states, counties and research clusters do not count as a shared locality, and fallback, broad representative or kin-inferred coordinates are excluded from distance scoring. Shared descendant profiles are removed before branch-name comparison. A candidate already recorded as a parent-in-law is excluded. A confident or independently supported parent is treated as settled; uncertain and unassessed attachments remain open to alternative comparison. A different linked parent, an uncle/aunt or grandparent path, and a matching existing child profile prevent an alternative from being classified as a strong direct-parent lead until the underlying tree conflict or duplicate is resolved. Familiar forms such as Bessie are normalised. Surname remains an eligibility filter worth zero points.
potential_parentage.warning: Naming customs, shared farms and occupations are circumstantial. Children, spouses and collateral relatives may be missing, and tree-derived family networks are not independent evidence. Scores rank research leads; they do not prove parentage.

profile_creation.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
John Glasgow was listed under the Glasgow heading in the Edinburgh apprenticeship register on 12 January 1648, as an apprentice to William Blackwood, merchant. The entry describes him as the son of “late Thomas G., maltman, burgess of Glasgow.” The father's surname is abbreviated in the line.<ref>Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583–1666'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1906), p. 75; FamilySearch, ''Edinburgh. Apprenticeship Records 1583–1666'', item #007764594, Item 3, image 101, entry under Glasgow; https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSM7-53ZS-V?view=fullText&keywords=Glasgow&searchForm=advanced&lang=en&groupId=M9H7-2TF. The printed register is a transcription; the original register was not examined.</ref>
== Research Notes ==
The date is the apprenticeship entry date, not a birth or death date. The entry gives no age, birthplace, spouse, children or later residence. Glasgow-1604, Glasgow-3145 and Glasgow-3610 remain possible existing identities by chronology, but no distinguishing link has been found. Do not attach this occurrence to an existing profile or create a second WikiTree profile until the identity is resolved.
